subject: Decision Making
title: Herbert Simon and Bounded Rationality
description: A quick, practical guide to Herbert Simon and Bounded Rationality.

hook.text: Herbert Simon said humans are not rational. We are boundedly rational: limited by time, data, and brainpower.

buildup.text: Classical economics assumed perfect information and unlimited processing. Simon said that is a fantasy.

discovery.text: He coined satisficing: choosing the first good-enough option instead of searching for the best possible one.

twist.text: Satisficing often beats optimizing. Perfect searches cost time and energy that exceed the value of a better choice.

climax.text: Simon won the Nobel Prize for showing that real decision-making is messy, fast, and good enough instead of perfect.

punchline.text: Good enough beats perfect. Simon proved that real decisions satisfice.

quiz.question: What does 'satisficing' mean?
options: Choosing the first good-enough option instead of optimizing
